title: IT / Finance / Security Ops Sync
summary: Quick ops sync to align IT, Finance, Security and Legal on upcoming SOC 2 controls, KMS rotations, billing allocation for new dedicated clusters, and procurement timing for reserved GPU capacity. Agreed to one-off benchmark for billing model, update SOC 2 evidence tracker, and legal to review contractual changes for Dedicated discounts.
action_items: Priya Kapoor | Produce updated chargeback spreadsheet with per-team usage buckets and proposed rates | 2025-11-10
Diego Morales | Rotate KMS keys for prod region and document rotation process in runbook | 2025-11-08
Lena Park | Draft amendment language for Dedicated reserved capacity discounts and term lengths | 2025-11-14
Avery Chen | Schedule sandbox VPC peering with infra team and run connectivity test | 2025-11-06
next_steps: Priya to share draft chargeback model and cost assumptions
Diego to confirm KMS rotation window and potential downtime impact
Lena to circulate legal redline for Dedicated contract amendment
Avery to book follow-up technical check-in next week to review VPC peering results
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-03 14:00 UTC — Duration 45 mins
Attendees: Avery Chen, Priya Kapoor, Diego Morales, Lena Park, Tom Nguyen
---
00:00:03 Avery: ok everyone, let's kick off, this is the IT / Finance / Security sync i think we have 45 minutes, uh quick round robin?
00:00:12 Priya: yeah, i'll start on finance side — we ran the preliminary numbers for october usage, saw a 12% uptick in dedicated cluster hours, mainly from marketing and the embeddings project. need to talk chargeback.
00:00:29 Diego: security — nothing urgent, but KMS rotation is due next week for prod region, and i want to confirm with it if any services will break. also SOC two evidence items, we have a couple overdue tickets.
00:00:45 Lena: legal — i'll need to draft amendment language for reserved capacity discounts, and confirm change to data processing addendum for the new privacy controls.
00:00:56 Tom: cfo quick note — procurement wants to know timeline if we move forward with more reserved capacity, need committed spend numbers by mid november.
00:01:10 Avery: cool, agenda for today: (1) cost allocation + chargeback, (2) soc 2 evidence and who owns what, (3) kms key rotation and impact, (4) vpc peering for sandbox accounts, and (5) procurement timeline for reserved capacity.

00:02:25 Priya: on chargeback — i created a spreadsheet, i've bucketed by team and by feature: hosted API, dedicated infra, and private deployments. main question is do we apply a flat per-GPU hour rate or tiered rates for reserved vs on-demand? the dedicated discount currently isn't modeled.
00:02:47 Tom: prefer modeled reserved vs on-demand because commit discounts change unit economics a lot. we should surface net cost to product lines so pm's know the threshold.
00:03:05 Diego: also consider including an ops tax for security/observability, like 5% for central infra costs. otherwise teams under-price their features and we miss centralized costs.
00:03:18 Priya: yeah i like that, i'll add an ops allocation line. question — any upcoming infra changes that would shift usage patterns?
00:03:30 Avery: we're planning a small pilot of a larger-batch scheduler in mid november that may change averaging. but it should reduce per-token compute, mostly affects throughput-oriented jobs.

00:04:15 Lena: on the contract side, if we offer multi-year discounts for dedicated, legal needs standard language around termination and data retention. also need to align with SOC two controls for access reviews.
00:04:28 Diego: speaking of SOC two — control A.9, i think the evidence for key management and rotation is incomplete. we have documented procedures but not all rotations logged in the evidence tracker.
00:04:41 Avery: is that the tracker in confluence?
00:04:44 Diego: yep, some entries are missing timestamps.
00:04:48 Priya: can we get a list of missing items? i can prioritize with finance ops to fill them.
00:04:55 Diego: i'll export the tracker and mark the missing ones by end of day.

00:06:12 Tom: procurement — timeline question. If we commit to additional dedicated capacity by Dec 1st, procurement needs final approval by Nov 20th. we need pricing and legal redlines well before that.
00:06:26 Lena: i'll aim to get a first draft redline by Nov 14th. can we confirm expected discount levels?
00:06:33 Priya: currently we're modeling a 20% discount for 12-month reserved commit in the spreadsheet, but that's rough.
00:06:41 Avery: ops note — when we talk about reserved capacity, ensure we include costs for telemetry retention, as dedicated clusters increase storage/observability spend.

00:07:55 Avery: KMS rotation details — Diego, what's the window and risk?
00:08:01 Diego: plan is to rotate primary keys in us-west-2 on tuesday midnight maintenance window, anticipated impact: brief re-encrypt operations, no expected downtime, but some older SDKs may fail if they cache keys. transcription note: some folks call it K-M-S or kms but i heard people say K M S wrong; also our runbook mentions HSM integration but sometimes it's typed as H-M-S.
00:08:27 Priya: do we need to notify teams?
00:08:29 Diego: yes, i'll send an email and post in #infra-alerts. i'll also include a checklist for services that need key refresh.
00:08:36 Avery: make sure we include the private deployment teams — they have on-prem key references that need manual rotation.

00:09:40 Priya: back on chargeback spreadsheets — i'm going to show a sample calc: total GPU hours * base rate -> then subtract reserved discount -> add ops allocation -> charge to teams. open question is whether to amortize committed spend over expected utilization vs booked commit.
00:10:01 Tom: amortize over expected utilization for internal reporting, but for billing teams we should show both amortized and cash-flow impact so product leaders see long-term unit economics.

00:11:20 Lena: legal question — if we amortize, do we need to reflect that in customer-facing docs?
00:11:25 Priya: no, this is internal chargeback. customer-facing pricing remains unchanged.
00:11:30 Lena: ok good.

00:12:05 Diego: SOC two follow-ups: i'll assign owners on the tracker to update access review screenshots and key rotation logs. some of the access evidence is stale because of the hr provisioning lag.
00:12:18 Avery: action: Diego to export tracker by EOD, Priya to help fill missing invoices and cost reports for evidentiary items.

00:13:50 Priya: any questions about the embeddings project's spend? marketing team requested burst capacity for a research eval, if we approve burst they'll go to on-demand which is expensive. should we require a PO?
00:14:04 Tom: yes require PO for any >$5k burst. procurement will sign off.

00:15:30 Avery: VPC peering for sandbox accounts — current state, sandbox runs in separate aws account and we occasionally need to test dedicated networking. i've asked infra to set up a peering but need security sign-off for route tables and flow logs.
00:15:47 Diego: flow logs must be enabled for peered connections, and we need to ensure sensitive logs aren't forwarded to public buckets. encryption in transit is fine but data residency concerns exist for eu sandboxes.
00:16:05 Lena: document any cross-account access in the sla. also ensure sso mappings and least privilege are enforced. we had a misnamed role last quarter that caused excess privilege.

00:17:20 Priya: cost modeling for peering — there will be inter-account data transfer charges if cross-region. need to estimate.
00:17:31 Avery: peering will be same region for now (us-west-2), so minimal outbound cost, but we'll monitor.

00:19:10 Diego: quick tech note — some teams use cached kv cache libraries that assume stable host keys; when we rotate kms keys, their cached tokens expire. i'll add a compatibility note in the runbook. (transcription glitch: speaker 3 sometimes listed as diego m. or speaker 2)

00:20:45 Priya: procurement asks for a one-pager with committed spend and expected utilization delta. i'll draft and ask Avery for the infra numbers.
00:20:55 Avery: i'll pull utilization by nov 6 and share the summary.

00:22:12 Lena: legal — on data processing addendum, need to reconcile new encryption language with customer obligations for private deployments. some older customer configs bypass our managed kms and we need to document control ownership.
00:22:30 Diego: right, private on-prem deployments often have customer-managed keys — ensure we don't overwrite or rotate those. add a section to the runbook for customer-managed key integration.

00:24:05 Priya: any blockers on the billing side?
00:24:08 Tom: nothing blocker, just timeline alignment.

00:25:30 Avery: let's do a quick walk through of the SOC two evidence list. Diego, can you call out highest priority missing items?
00:25:38 Diego: highest priority: key rotation logs, access review screenshots for oct, two MFA exception tickets that need closure, and one pen test remediation evidence doc.
00:25:51 Priya: i can coordinate with security to attach invoices and payment proof for pen-test vendor.

00:27:10 Lena: for MFA exceptions, legal wants to see documented compensating controls before we sign any contracts that rely on those exceptions.
00:27:20 Diego: agreed — i'll close tickets or document compensating controls in the tracker.

00:29:00 Priya: chargeback model preview: i'm proposing showing three views — current month actuals, 12m amortized commit, and forecast with proposed rates. open question: do we show per-token cost or per-GPU-hour? Some product leads prefer per-token.
00:29:20 Tom: per-token is useful for product, but ops and finance need per-GPU-hour for capacity planning. include both.

00:31:15 Avery: benchmarking ask — product wants a short benchmark comparing current dedicated perf vs a new batch scheduler; that'll inform the model. can we schedule a 2-hour benchmark next week?
00:31:28 Priya: yes, but need sign-off on cost floor for running the benchmark.
00:31:33 Tom: ok set a $2k cap and get approval if it goes beyond.

00:32:50 Diego: small note — some transcribed names in the tracker are wrong (redwood product names like Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as red-wood dedicated or red moon ded. just flagging for the SOC two evidence exports).

00:34:05 Priya: i'll update the spreadsheet and annotate assumptions.

00:35:40 Avery: wrap up time — quick recap and owners. Priya to share draft chargeback and one-pager by nov 10, Diego to rotate kms and export tracker by nov 8, Lena to send legal redline by nov 14, Avery to schedule follow-up tech check and share utilization by nov 6.
00:35:58 Tom: procurement will need final numbers by nov 20 if we're to commit by dec 1.
00:36:10 Priya: noted.
00:36:25 Diego: i'll post an infra runbook link in slack after rotation.
00:36:30 Avery: any other items?
00:36:33 Lena: one micro ask — confirm who on- call is next week in case rotation causes alerts.
00:36:39 Avery: on-call is me and jess for infra. i'll ping them.
00:36:45 Priya: thanks everyone.
00:36:49 Avery: meeting adjourned.
---
Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., KMS spelled K M S or H-M-S); speaker labels inconsistent in a few segments; timestamps approximate.
